React compact chip uses a black background with yellow text and a right-aligned pink notification dot; Android variants share the same yellow banner shape but differ in icon, label, and internal layout.

Android 'SETTINGS OFF' variant shows the titlebar extended to the full width with a leading pink dot clipping outside the right edge; React compact chip is left-aligned with extra right padding and the pink dot sits inside the chip.

Android '32dp square · custom' variant adds a leading pixel-art icon (blue/white) before the title; '32dp square · fallback' variant shows a black square with letter 'R'. React has no leading icon slot.

Android 'Expanded switcher' panel includes sub-labels ('/raft-design', '/raft-community'), a checkmark on the selected row, and a secondary 'Raft Community' row; React has no switcher/expanded state at all.

Android implementation expanded the titlebar spec to include leading icon slot, fallback avatar, expanded switcher list, and sub-label — features not yet present in the React component.

If the Android additions are intentional, generate React baselines for each variant (settings off, 32dp custom, 32dp fallback, expanded switcher) and update the states spec in the design system.
Match titlebar vertical metrics: anchor leading icon padding, label baseline, and trailing dot offset to the same dp values across platforms.
Add the expanded switcher (with sub-label /workspace and checkmark indicator) to the React implementation, or mark it as Android-only in the spec.
Verify the pink unread-indicator dot position: on Android it floats outside the chip's right edge, on React it sits inside — pick one and enforce via shared token.

intentional: Pink notification dot position and color (right of the warning badge) is consistent across both platforms and appears intentional.

summary: Result count and result set differ: React shows '3 RESULTS' with one channel result and two message results; Android shows '5 results' with two entity results (channel + DM) and three message results, plus a 'Load more results' button.

Filter row layout divergence: React renders a two-row wrapping chip group including 'Recent' sort chip and 'Clear All'; Android renders a single non-wrapping row with fewer, fully-populated filter chips (From: Me, Scope 2, #design). Documented as intentional platform difference.
DM/Agent result card present on Android only: 'Android Developer' DM card with 'Agent · @Android-Developer · Members' subline has no counterpart on React.

Channel result metadata differs: React's 'android-artifacts' row shows just 'Channel'; Android adds a 'Builds and screenshots' description line and uses different label placement for the 'Channel' tag.

Message card timestamps and structure differ: React uses relative time ('20 days ago'); Android uses clock timestamps (10:38, 10:31, 09:58) and one message carries a 'Thread #design 2 hits' header with a pink/highlighted background, which is absent on React.
likelyCauses: Search API response size or pagination state differs between React and Android clients (Android fetched additional entities and messages).
Filter chip component uses different wrapping/count policies per platform, producing different result-set previews.
Locale/time formatting differs: React formats relative dates, Android formats absolute HH:MM.
DM entity result type is rendered on Android but not yet implemented or filtered out on React.
Threaded-message variant with hits-summary header is a React-not-yet-adopted component currently shipping on Android.
suggestedFixes: Reconcile result-set contract: ensure both clients paginate and aggregate channel, DM, and message results identically; add a shared fixtures/contract test.
Unify filter chip behavior to a documented platform rule and surface the same active filter set on both sides (or accept divergence in design system).
Pick one timestamp formatting (relative vs absolute) or align by platform rules so both sides read consistently.
Add the DM/Agent result card to the React search results list, or explicitly exclude DM entity results on both platforms.
Decide on the threaded-message-with-hits card: either back-port to React or document as Android-only and update visual baselines.
intentional: Filter chip row count, wrap, and presence of the sort/Recent chip differs between React (multi-row) and Android (single row) — intentional mobile-vs-web platform divergence mirroring tasks.panel filter-row declaration.

cases.title: Home Search Channel Dropdown

summary: Channel dropdown is open on Android (right) but closed on React (left); React shows a static '# Channel' selector with no flyout, while Android renders an open panel with search input, item list, selected check, and DM entry.

Filter chip row differs: React shows partial chips ('From', 'Scope', 'Channel', 'Any Time', 'Relevant') clipped at left edge with no icons; Android shows fully visible '@ From: Me', '@ Scope 2', '# #design' chips on a yellow filled background plus a back arrow icon in the search bar.

Selected channel indicator is missing on Android (no 'android-artifacts selected' CHANN... badge) and Android instead shows a small inline checkmark next to '#design' in the dropdown, while React has a yellow left bar on the selected row.

Main content area layout diverges: React renders a left-aligned 'RESULTS / CHANNELS & DMS' header and message cards clipped to the left half of the viewport; Android renders full-width cards with avatars, timestamps, thread indicators, and a 'Load more results' button.
Primary search action differs: React search input has a clear (×) icon button on the right; Android replaces it with a back arrow on the left and omits the inline clear button.
likelyCauses: Android and React implementations diverge in the search screen's initial state: Android opens the dropdown on render while React renders collapsed selectors.
Different filter chip specs between platforms — Android uses filled yellow chips with full labels and icons; React uses outlined chips with truncated labels and no prefix icons.

Result list rendering is built from different components per platform: Android pulls MessageItem/ThreadMessageItem with avatars, timestamps, and a Load more action; React renders a simplified card list without those affordances.
Search input accessory icons differ (back vs clear), indicating separate top-bar implementations per platform.
suggestedFixes: Align the initial dropdown state across platforms: either show it open on both or closed on both, and match the selected channel indicator (yellow accent bar vs checkmark).
Unify filter chip design — same filled vs outlined treatment, full label visibility, and leading '@' / '#' icons in both React and Android.
Normalize search input accessory: pick one (back arrow or clear button) and apply consistently across platforms.
Reuse the shared MessageItem/ThreadMessageItem component on React (or add a React equivalent) so author, avatar, timestamp, thread badge, and Load more appear identically.
Define a shared design token set for chip background color, selected-row indicator, card padding, and avatar size to enforce parity.

summary: Title 'Set up your account' on iOS is noticeably bolder/heavier weight than Android (Android uses a lighter, more rounded sans-serif; iOS uses a heavier weight closer to Bold).

Form input fields (Username, Display name) and the 'Continue' button on iOS have thicker, double-stacked outlines / heavier borders with a visible drop-shadow offset (bottom-right shadow), whereas Android shows a single thin black border without shadow.

All body/label/helper text on iOS appears slightly larger and tighter to the baseline; helper text 'Your unique name for @mentions and links. It can't be changed later.' wraps onto one line on iOS but wraps to two lines on Android due to different widths/font metrics.

Content block on iOS is shifted further down the canvas and has more vertical breathing room between the header band, icon, title, and inputs compared to Android, producing a looser top-to-bottom rhythm.
likelyCauses: Kuikly is falling back to a different system font on iOS (likely SF Pro / system Bold) versus Android (Roboto / lighter weight), causing weight and metric divergence.

Default border and elevation/styling on iOS is being interpreted with a double-stroke + shadow effect (possibly a focus/active border style or a shadow compositing artifact) rather than the single 1px stroke used on Android.
Missing platform-specific token mapping in the shared Kuikly theme for input border, button shadow, and title typography weight.
No normalization applied for device pixel ratio differences (1170x2532 vs 390x844) so dp-based sizes scale differently across the two renders.
suggestedFixes: Define explicit font-family, font-weight (e.g., SemiBold 600) for the screen title in the shared token set so both platforms render identical weight.
Normalize input and button border to a single 1px stroke with no shadow; if a shadow is intended, move it to an explicit elevation token applied identically on both platforms.
Ensure the helper text field has a fixed min-width or uses the same wrap behavior on both platforms (consider truncating/allowing wrap via shared style).
Re-run Slock with aligned DPR (render iOS at logical 390x844) so pixel mismatch from raw canvas size does not amplify small font/border differences.
Add a visual regression check for border thickness and text weight parity across Android/iOS in CI.

Avatar status-indicator overlay missing in Android implementation.
Mention/reference token styling (pill background, border-radius, fill color) not ported to Android markup styles.

Re-add orange online-status dot to the avatar in Android MessageRow.
Restore pill background (yellow for @mention, pink for #reference) with correct corner radius in Android Compose styling.

likelyCauses: Different default font sizes and line-heights between web (React) and iOS UITextView/UILabel rendering.

CJK punctuation-aware line breaking rules differ between browser text layout and iOS NSLineBreakStrategy, causing earlier wrap on iOS.
suggestedFixes: Normalize typography tokens (font-size, line-height, letter-spacing) for message body and metadata across React and iOS using a shared design system value, not platform defaults.
Share or replicate the avatar asset; until then ensure iOS uses a consistent placeholder that matches the React design intent.
Unify timestamp formatting through a single locale-aware formatter and remove stray 'K' character; explicitly include/exclude AM/PM token per spec.
Define a single markdown inline-highlight pill spec (padding, radius, border, background) and consume it on both platforms.
Apply consistent CJK line-breaking behavior — consider explicitly inserting soft line breaks before full-width punctuation or using a shared line-break strategy setting.
